question: A single ultrasound showing polycystic ovarian morphology (PCOM) is sufficient to diagnose PCOS without requiring clinical or biochemical criteria.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: Correct — this statement is false. PCOM is one of three Rotterdam criteria; the diagnosis requires at least two criteria. Up to 25% of normal women may show PCOM on ultrasound without having PCOS.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: That is not correct. PCOM is only ONE of three Rotterdam criteria. A diagnosis of PCOS requires at least TWO of: oligo/anovulation, clinical/biochemical hyperandrogenism, and PCOM. The scan alone cannot diagnose PCOS.
